sources.title: Greenland: History and Society
sources.note: University of Greenland synthesis on monopoly trade, sealing policy, colonial hierarchy, literacy, intermediaries, and national awakening.

sources.title: Greenland: Literature and Cultural Production
sources.note: University of Greenland synthesis on oral history, print, visual counter-narratives, early novels, colonial censorship, and political imagination.

sources.title: The Socioeconomic Development of Greenland
sources.note: University of Greenland account of trade, administration, population, and the 1911 municipal and provincial councils.

sources.title: From Provincial Councils to Parliament to Inatsisartut
sources.note: Official parliamentary history of the 1908 act, two administrative regions, first 1911 meetings, and advisory limits.

sources.title: The colonial period until the war years
sources.note: Expert-authored Greenland history covering the 1905 law, 1908 reform, 1911 councils, East Greenland, and Thule station.

sources.title: Greenland's Building Culture and History
sources.note: Greenland National Museum account of turf houses, shared rooms, trading-post buildings, changing windows, and the Nuuk seminary.

sources.title: Building customs and architecture in Greenland
sources.note: Expert architectural history distinguishing early family homes from much later houses designed with separate toilets and installed water.

sources.title: Missionaries and catechists official diaries
sources.note: Greenland National Archives guide to catechist teaching and Greenlandic work diaries from about 1880 to 1930.

sources.title: Gustav Olsen's Thule diaries, 1909 to 1920
sources.note: Greenland National Archives description of Olsen, Ane Sophie, teaching, population lists, and Thule outside the colony.

sources.title: Aasiviit
sources.note: Greenland National Museum account of seasonal gathering, barter, news, conflict resolution, courtship, and changing mobility.

sources.title: Lifestyle and class distinctions
sources.note: Greenland National Museum interpretation of colonial ethnic hierarchy, export sealing, disease, imported skills, and limited training.

sources.title: Inuit means of transport
sources.note: Greenland National Museum overview of qajaqs, umiaqs, dog sledges, tools, regional adaptation, and twentieth-century continuity.

sources.title: Ammerineq: knowledge of skin treatment
sources.note: Greenland National Museum account of curing skins and using sinew, membrane, stomach, and hide for equipment and clothing.

sources.title: Dogs in Greenland
sources.note: Greenland National Museum history of regional dog use and the 1907 rules separating sled-dog and other dog zones.

sources.title: Municipal councils archive guide
sources.note: Greenland National Archives guide to the 1911 replacement of boards by northern and southern municipal and provincial councils.

sources.title: Qaanaaq history
sources.note: Expert account of Inughuit territory, the private 1910 Thule station, and its status outside the old colonial districts.

sources.title: Tasiilaq history
sources.note: Expert regional history of East Greenland contact, the 1894 station, scattered settlement, hunting, and transport constraints.

sources.title: Religion and religious communities in Greenland
sources.note: Expert account of the 1909 Thule mission, Gustav Olsen, and the first Inughuit baptisms in 1912.

sources.title: Agriculture in Greenland
sources.note: Expert history of Jens Chemnitz introducing Faroese sheep in 1906 and the limited early South Greenland experiment.

sources.title: The 1919 to 1921 influenza pandemic in Greenland
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of church records, incomplete medical certification, colonial diagnoses, and early twentieth-century disease evidence.

sources.title: Patients and doctors in Greenland seventy years ago and today
sources.note: Medical-history abstract on 1924 district care, sled transport, hospital limits, crowding, hunger, and tuberculosis.

sources.title: Greenlandic water and sanitation: a context-oriented analysis
sources.note: Peer-reviewed historical review showing the long regional and infrastructural variation of water and sanitation systems.

sources.title: Mathias Storch: Sinnattugaq
sources.note: Greenland National Library digital edition and description of the 1914 first Greenlandic novel and its original title.

sources.title: Language in Greenland
sources.note: Expert history of Greenlandic writing, early twentieth-century authors, orthographic change, and Sinnattugaq in 1914.

sources.title: Nunarput utoqqarsuanngoravit
sources.note: Danish songbook text identifying Henrik Lund's Greenlandic words as written in 1912 and supplying the original lines.

sources.title: Danish Arctic Institute photo collections
sources.note: Archive guide to over 300,000 Arctic photographs, especially the 1890 to 1960 record of Greenlandic society.

sources.title: Uummannaq in the Thule station era, 1910 to 1950
sources.note: Greenland National Museum teaching source on Inughuit families, seasonal movement, traded goods, and housing around the station.

sources.title: Sources for the history of the Greenland mission to the 1905 Church and School Act
sources.note: Danish Historical Source Society guide to administrative sources and the first unified church and school regulation.

sources.title: The Greenlandic Sled Dog
sources.note: Greenland National Museum account of oral skill transmission, regional sled designs, seasonal work, and dog-human cooperation.
